title: Willie Cornish and Buddy Collins
summary: The interviewer asks about trumpet players of the Bolden band era; Lewis names Willie Cornish and recalls Buddy Collins, in largely garbled text.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Um, you mentioned, uh, first you could talk about some of these real time that you knew. You know, I'd like to mention this guy that played with the South Podium band, uh, Yeah, uh, The Father I... Uh... Uh...

It wasn't Willie Cornish, it was a company. Yeah, Willie Cornish. Willie Cornish. Willie Cornish. Willie Cornish. He played, we played together, wasn't it? The Eurico, where's Eurico band? I played with him. Uh...
I'm trying to remember the name of another trumpet player. I'm trying to think of the name of the supposed to be another trumpet player, with both, but I just can't remember his name.

Well, I mean, it might have been a man, you know, but this particular picture, which you see in the magazine, that's, uh, uh, for the carnage. I think some of them men, I had one picture with, uh, old man Jimmy Johnson, Biggs, and I played with him. He lived up there around about a two-door, and it's called the 24th. Well, he went to Georgia, and he played with Don Redmond, Don Edgert, Don Alva's band. And, uh, a young boy was, a young man was called Buddy Collins. He went somewhere to Georgia to beat him up upon the boys' way. And, uh, Buddy Collins didn't live six months after that. And Buddy Jones, he died also after. I think Alva was playing with a band there. He caught him on the highway and just beat him up for his family and nothing at all.
Didn't you say that Collins was sort of like a friend of the family or something like that?

What sort of style did he play on?
